BUILD SLICE S1 OF THE V3 COLONY PLANNER: THE PURE `cpe` CORE (CP BUDGET AND PORT-ORDER CALCULATOR). PYTHON ONLY. NO API ROUTE, NO DATABASE, NO WEB CHANGE.

Authority: the V3 Colony Planner design, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md, which is in open PR #924 (branch docs/v3-colony-planner-design) and not yet on main: read it with `git fetch origin docs/v3-colony-planner-design && git show FETCH_HEAD:docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-v3-colony-planner-design.md` (sections 4, 5.1 and 7), but everything this slice needs is restated below and this text wins if they differ. Also docs/ROADMAP.md owner decisions D2/D3 (2026-10-21). Do not copy the design or roadmap edits into this branch. Rules come from the pinned CRE rulebook docs/reference/colonisation/cre-rulebook/rulebook.json (cre-knowledge-v0.3.0) and the bundled facility catalogue apps/api/src/domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json. Raven Colonial is GPL-3.0: do not copy, translate or vendor anything from it, and do not look it up.

Do NOT touch: optimiser/, simulation/, routers/, recommendations/, regional/, packages/planner-core, apps/web/, sql/, Ratings V4 code (domain/ratings_v4*.py), the facility catalogue JSON, cp_rules.py's formulas, or any Finder code. Do not add dependencies.

FILES TO ADD (all under apps/api/src/cpe/ unless stated):

1. __init__.py — short docstring naming the design file; re-export the public API: Plan, Site, Body, evaluate_plan, rule, RULEBOOK_RELEASE.

2. data/rulebook.json — a byte-for-byte copy of docs/reference/colonisation/cre-rulebook/rulebook.json (use cp; do not re-serialise).

3. rules.py — load data/rulebook.json once (functools.cache) via Path(__file__).parent / 'data' / 'rulebook.json'. Expose: RULEBOOK_RELEASE (the file's release_tag), a frozen dataclass Rule(id, topic, title, status, statement, quote, page) where quote/page come from the rule's first source entry, and rule(rule_id) -> Rule raising KeyError for an unknown id.

4. catalogue.py — the planner's own read-only catalogue.
   a. In apps/api/src/domain/facilities.py add ONE public pure function templates_from_json_data(data) -> dict[str, FacilityTemplate] that converts every template with the existing _template_json_to_row + FacilityTemplate.from_db_row and returns a new dict WITHOUT touching the module global _CATALOGUE; make load_catalogue_from_json_data use it (behaviour unchanged). This is the only change outside cpe/ apart from tests.
   b. catalogue.py reads domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json (path via the facilities module's _BUNDLED_CATALOGUE_PATH or an equivalent Path) with templates_from_json_data, cached once, and NEVER calls get_catalogue()/get_facility()/load_*. Exclude colony_ship (use facilities.is_colony_ship). Expose planner_facilities() -> Mapping[str, FacilityTemplate] (read-only, e.g. types.MappingProxyType) and facility(facility_id) raising KeyError.
   c. Structured prerequisites. Define PREREQUISITE_FACILITY_IDS: dict[str, frozenset[str]] mapping each exact catalogue prerequisite description to the facility ids that satisfy it (ANY one satisfies). Use exactly this table (an arrow "A ➔ B" is a chain; the direct prerequisite is the LAST element, which itself requires the earlier one):
      'Settlement - Research Bio' -> surface_settlement_research_bio_t1_m, surface_settlement_research_bio_t1_s, surface_settlement_research_bio_t2_l
      'Settlement - Military' -> surface_settlement_military_t1_m, surface_settlement_military_t1_s, surface_settlement_military_t2_l
      'Installation - Relay Station' -> orbital_installation_relay_station
      'Satellite ➔ Tourism Settlement' -> surface_settlement_tourism_t1_m, surface_settlement_tourism_t1_s, surface_settlement_tourism_t2_l
      'Settlement - Extraction' -> surface_settlement_extraction_t1_m, surface_settlement_extraction_t1_s, surface_settlement_extraction_t2_l
      'Settlement - Agriculture' -> surface_settlement_agriculture_t1_m, surface_settlement_agriculture_t1_s, surface_settlement_agriculture_t2_l
      'Installation - Space Farm' -> orbital_installation_space_farm
      'Installation - Mining Outpost' -> orbital_installation_mining_outpost
      'Mil. Settlement ➔ Mil. Installation' -> orbital_installation_military
      'Installation - Comm Station' -> orbital_installation_comm_station
      'Installation - Satellite' -> orbital_installation_satellite
   Expose prerequisites_for(facility_id) -> tuple[frozenset[str], ...] (one entry per catalogue prerequisite; all entries must be satisfied; within an entry any id satisfies). If a catalogue prerequisite description is not in the table, raise at load time (fail closed).

5. plan.py — frozen dataclasses and validation.
   - Body(body_ref: str, orbital_slots: int | None, surface_slots: int | None, is_landable: bool | None, is_ringed: bool | None). None means unknown.
   - Site(site_id: str, facility_id: str, body_ref: str | None, slot_kind: Literal['orbital','surface'], status: Literal['planned','building','complete','demolished'], name: str | None = None).
   - Plan(system_id64: int, bodies: tuple[Body, ...], sites: tuple[Site, ...]). List order is the build order; sites[0] is the Primary Port.
   - validate_plan(plan) -> list[PlanIssue] (PlanIssue(code, site_id | None, message)). Bounds and codes: system_id64 in 1..2**63-1 (BAD_SYSTEM); 1..300 sites (TOO_MANY_SITES / NO_SITES); at most 1000 bodies (TOO_MANY_BODIES); unique site_id 1..64 chars (BAD_SITE_ID); name None or <= 64 chars (BAD_NAME); facility_id in planner_facilities() (UNKNOWN_FACILITY); body_ref None or present in bodies (UNKNOWN_BODY); slot counts None or 0..64 (BAD_SLOTS); slot_kind must suit the facility: orbital or ringed_orbital facilities need 'orbital', surface facilities need 'surface', orbital_or_surface accepts either (LOCATION_MISMATCH); sites[0] must be a port (FacilityTemplate.is_port) and must not be demolished (PRIMARY_NOT_PORT / PRIMARY_DEMOLISHED). evaluate_plan refuses (raises PlanInvalid carrying the issues) when any issue exists.

6. budget.py and checks.py — evaluate_plan(plan) -> Evaluation. Semantics (keep exactly; each is a design rule):
   - Escalation uses mechanics.cp_rules only: escalating_port_tier(template), t2_port_yellow_cost(n), t3_port_green_cost(n). n is ONE shared 1-based counter over Tier 2 and Tier 3 escalating ports, in list order, excluding the Primary Port. A port advances n when its construction starts (status building or complete, or a planned step that passes). Demolished sites and BLOCKED planned steps never advance n and count for nothing.
   - Cost of a site: Primary Port 0/0 (RB-0004). Escalating T2 port: yellow t2_port_yellow_cost(n), green 0. Escalating T3 port: green t3_port_green_cost(n), yellow 0 (RB-0003, RB-0005, RB-0006). Anything else: its catalogue yellow_cp_cost / green_cp_cost (RB-0002). Rewards: catalogue yellow_cp_generated / green_cp_generated, Primary Port included.
   - "now" view: walk only complete and building sites in list order. Costs are charged for both; rewards only for complete. No blocking: negative totals are reported as they are.
   - "after_plan" view: start from the "now" totals, then add the rewards of every building site (they are assumed to finish first), then walk the planned sites in list order. For each planned site compute its cost at the current n, then check:
       BLOCKED reasons (step skipped, walk continues): INSUFFICIENT_T2 / INSUFFICIENT_T3 when the cost of that tier is > 0 and the running total is below it (a zero cost never blocks, even when the total is negative); PREREQUISITE_MISSING when some prerequisites_for entry has no satisfying site that is complete, building, or an earlier passed planned step; NO_FREE_SLOT when the body's slot count of that kind is known and complete + building + earlier passed planned sites on that body and kind already fill it; NOT_LANDABLE when a surface site's body has is_landable False; NOT_RINGED when a ringed_orbital facility's body has is_ringed False.
       NEEDS_INFO reasons (step assumed to go ahead and says so): NOT_PLACED (body_ref None), SLOTS_UNKNOWN, LANDABLE_UNKNOWN, RINGED_UNKNOWN.
       Otherwise OK. A passing step (OK or NEEDS_INFO) pays its cost, then adds its reward (planned steps are taken one at a time, each finishing before the next), and advances n if it is an escalating port.
   - Plan-level checks (reported in Evaluation.plan_checks, not per step): MORE_THAN_FIVE_BUILDING when more than five sites have status building (RB-0007).
   - Evaluation (frozen dataclasses, JSON-friendly): rulebook_release; now = Totals(t2, t3); after_plan = Totals(t2, t3); steps: one StepResult per site in list order with site_id, facility_id, status, view ('now' | 'after_plan' | 'ignored' for demolished), result ('OK' | 'BLOCKED' | 'NEEDS_INFO' | 'COUNTED' for now-view sites | 'IGNORED'), counted_port_number (int or None), cost_t2, cost_t3, reward_t2, reward_t3, t2_before, t3_before, t2_after, t3_after, reasons (tuple of codes), rule_ids (tuple), payers (tuple of facility ids, see below); plan_checks; summary counts per result; next_port_cost: the cost a further Tier 2 port and a further Tier 3 port would have after the whole plan (n + 1).
   - rule_ids per step: Primary Port ('RB-0004',); escalating port ('RB-0003','RB-0005','RB-0006'); other costed or rewarding sites ('RB-0002',); add 'RB-0007' to plan_checks entries. Prerequisite reasons cite no rule id (catalogue data).
   - payers (the "what pays for this" helper, a lookup, not an optimiser): only for INSUFFICIENT_T2/INSUFFICIENT_T3 steps. List up to 5 planner facility ids that are not escalating ports (cp_rules.escalating_port_tier is None), generate at least 1 point of the missing tier, cost 0 of that same tier, and whose location fits at least one body with a known free slot of the right kind at that point in the walk; sort by points generated (desc), then facility id. Empty tuple when none fit.

7. explain.py — explain_rule(rule_id) -> dict(id, title, status, statement, quote, page) built from rules.rule, and explain_step(step) -> list of those dicts for its rule_ids.

TESTS (under tests/, import with sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'apps' / 'api' / 'src')) then `from edfinder_api.cpe import ...`, as tests/test_cre_rulebook_parity.py does for its imports, with `# noqa: E402` on imports after the sys.path line (do not edit pyproject.toml); inside apps/api/src/cpe use `from edfinder_api.domain import facilities` and `from edfinder_api.mechanics import cp_rules`, matching the rest of apps/api/src):

A. tests/test_cpe_boundary.py — AST-scan every .py under apps/api/src/cpe/. Allowed imports: Python stdlib (sys.stdlib_module_names), __future__, relative imports within cpe, edfinder_api.cpe.*, edfinder_api.domain.facilities, edfinder_api.mechanics.cp_rules. Anything else fails, naming the file and import. Also assert no .py file under cpe/ mentions asyncpg, fastapi, optimiser, simulation or routers (data/rulebook.json is not scanned).

B. tests/test_cpe_rulebook_copy.py — sha256 of apps/api/src/cpe/data/rulebook.json equals pin.json's sha256 and equals the docs copy's bytes; RULEBOOK_RELEASE == pin.json release_tag; rule('RB-0003').status == 'Extracted'; rule('RB-9999') raises KeyError.

C. tests/test_cpe_catalogue.py — every catalogue prerequisite description is in PREREQUISITE_FACILITY_IDS and every mapped id exists in the catalogue; colony_ship excluded; planner_facilities() is read-only; cpe results are identical when domain.facilities' shared _CATALOGUE is empty, loaded from the bundled JSON, or loaded with a deliberately different row set (load_catalogue_from_rows with one altered template), proving cpe never reads it (restore the shared catalogue in a finally block); load_catalogue_from_json_data still fills _CATALOGUE exactly as before.

D. tests/test_cpe_budget.py — at least these cases, each asserting exact numbers:
   1. Primary Coriolis complete alone: no cost, rewards counted, n not advanced.
   2. Primary T1 outpost complete, then Coriolis, Coriolis, Orbis, Coriolis, Coriolis, Coriolis all complete: costs follow t2 3,3 / t3 12 / t2 7,9,11 with n = 1..6 (shared counter), proving the sixth counted port is 11 T2 points (RB-0003; Raven shows 12, the design notes the difference).
   3. Building port is charged and advances n but earns nothing in "now"; in "after_plan" its reward is added before planned steps.
   4. Demolished port: no cost, no reward, no n.
   5. Planned port short of T3 points is BLOCKED with INSUFFICIENT_T3, does not advance n, the next planned T2 port gets the n the blocked one would have had, and payers lists only non-escalating T3 earners that fit a free slot.
   6. Zero-cost T1 site with negative running totals is OK (never blocked by a zero cost).
   7. Industrial hub (industrial_facility) planned before any mining outpost is BLOCKED PREREQUISITE_MISSING; placed after a planned orbital_installation_mining_outpost it is OK; with the mining outpost status building it is OK.
   8. Military hub (military_installation) needs orbital_installation_military, not just a military settlement.
   9. Slots: known orbital_slots=2 with one complete orbital site and two planned orbital sites -> second planned is NO_FREE_SLOT; unknown slots -> NEEDS_INFO SLOTS_UNKNOWN and the step still pays and earns.
   10. Surface site on is_landable False -> NOT_LANDABLE; None -> LANDABLE_UNKNOWN. Asteroid base on is_ringed False -> NOT_RINGED; None -> RINGED_UNKNOWN.
   11. Six building sites -> plan_checks has MORE_THAN_FIVE_BUILDING with RB-0007.
   12. validate_plan codes: each code above has a failing example; evaluate_plan raises PlanInvalid.
   13. next_port_cost after a plan matches cp_rules for n + 1.
   14. Every rule id emitted by evaluate_plan resolves with rules.rule and explain_rule returns its quote.

E. tests/test_cpe_raven_answer_key.py — the branch already contains tests/fixtures/cpe/raven_answer_key_praea_euq_rev174.json (do not edit it). Load it, build a Plan from sites_in_raven_order (system_id64 from source, no bodies, every body_ref None, site_id/facility_id/slot_kind/status/name as given), run evaluate_plan, and assert now == expected.completed_sites_only (t2 1, t3 -17) and after_plan == expected.all_sites (t2 5, t3 -16). Also assert the fixture's known_differences entry is present, so the sixth-port difference stays recorded.
